facts.raw_span: A patient with high myopia was examined
The axial length was 30.0 mm
a yellowish oval lesion within a wide area of chorioretinal atrophy
a ringlike low reflectance pattern
a focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina
The sclera was approximately one-third thinner
98, 77, and 50 μm for the pit's floor, temporal wall, and nasal wall, respectively
The choroid was obliterated
Width and depth of 522 × 536 μm
The pit had a homogeneous low autofluorescence
Showed a branch of a posterior ciliary artery near the lesion
The pit was slightly hyperfluorescent in the late frames

concepts.why: High myopia and chorioretinal atrophy are characteristic of pathologic myopia
Focal scleral ectasia with thinning of the sclera is a key feature of this condition
Obliteration of the choroid is a significant finding in this case
The presence of a focal scleral ectasia with no overlying retina is consistent with posterior staphyloma
The ringlike low reflectance pattern, homogeneous low autofluorescence, and slight hyperfluorescence in the late frames are indicative of a macular hole.
The presence of a branch of a posterior ciliary artery near the lesion is consistent with peripapillary staphyloma.
